messages:
marta_support: Escalation from customer: they're hitting 429s on their Dedicated pool during short bursts (streaming responses). They say they have a reserved pool 4x standard, SLA shows headroom but requests still 429.
olivia_custsuccess: customer reported latency spikes then a string of 429s for ~3m, losing user sessions. Billing flagged request surge too. They really want a quick mitigation plan.jon_oncall: Can you paste a sample request/response (headers + X-RateLimit headers) and the pool id? Also which model variant are they pinned to?marta_support: Pool ID: rp-48a7, model: llm-xlarge-v2-q4f32 (streaming enabled).

Sample response headers we captured:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1718460100
X-ReservedPool-Id: rp-48a7
X-Consumed-Units: 1224
```

marta_support: Note: limit 600 looks like per-minute token-unit cap; their bursts push concurrent streams and per-connection accounting seems higher.

jon_oncall: Are they using streaming chunked responses? If we count per-connection overhead + prefix caching, effective units can be higher than expected with many small streams.

vikram_runtime: digging into serving logs for rp-48a7 — I see repeated entries where a single long-running session increments consumed units in micro-bursts. Possible cause: our streaming accounting double-counts KV-prefetch for each new connection if the client reconnects often.

vikram_runtime: quick repro hypothesis: many clients open N concurrent streams that each request small deltas; runtime charges an initial KV-prefetch + first-token overhead per connection. If concurrency spikes, this pushes them above the minute window even if avg QPS looks fine.

marta_support: Customer says their frontend retries on socket drop and opens new stream each retry (3 retries default). That would amplify the headroom burn.

jon_oncall: Ok — mitigation options:
- short-term: flip pool to allow burst headroom (admin flag) or temporarily increase reserved capacity
- immediate fallback: route to hosted fallback model for overflow
- medium: recommend client-side coalescing of small streams, reduce retries, or use longer-lived sessions

olivia_custsuccess: Customer prefers config change on our side first. They asked if we can enable a temporary burst allowance while we investigate.

vikram_runtime: I can enable burst_headroom=true for rp-48a7 for 30m (manual override) — that will allow a 2x transient multiplier on per-minute units. That should stop 429s while we fix accounting. I'll also add an alert to watch X-Consumed-Units.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by vikram_runtime — enabling burst_headroom for rp-48a7 (change-id ch-2026-11) :rocket:

deploy-bot: change applied to rp-48a7 — burst_headroom=true — effective now.

marta_support: telling customer; sending repro steps so they can test.

marta_support: Repro steps for customer / SRE team:
1) run a load generator with N concurrent streams (start N=100, then ramp to 400) using streaming chunk sizes 64-128 tokens
2) capture response headers and X-Consumed-Units for each request
3) check for per-connection reconnections (socket close/reopen) in client logs

Example curl snippet for header capture (non-streaming example):
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" \
  -d '{"model":"llm-xlarge-v2-q4f32","input":"test"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

jon_oncall: Also add this query on metrics stack to watch the short window burn:
```
sum(rate(dedicated_consumed_units_total{pool="rp-48a7"}[1m])) by (pool)
```

vikram_runtime: I pulled a 10m window before/after change — consumed units dropped to expected baseline after enabling burst flag. Looks promising, but we still need to fix double-counting on reconnects.

olivia_custsuccess: Customer confirmed 20m after we enabled burst they no longer see 429s and sessions restored. They asked for root cause and a timeline for the permanent fix.

vikram_runtime: Plan:
- short term: keep burst_headroom true for 48h while we patch accounting (we'll revert after patch deploy and run synthetic load tests)
- fix: adjust streaming accounting so KV-prefetch isn't recharged on reconnects within a 10s grace window; add unit tests and e2e
- rollout: canary to 10% of pools, then full rollout over 24h

jon_oncall: I'll own the rollback/monitor playbook and create alerts for any sustained >1m delta from baseline.

marta_support: I'll schedule customer touchpoint with olivia in 24h and share postmortem once fix lands. Thanks team :thumbsup:

olivia_custsuccess: assigning follow-ups: vikram -> runtime patch, jon -> monitor/playbook, marta -> customer comms. Will update CRM ticket.

marta_support: closing loop for now, re-open if 429s recur.

jon_oncall: noted. Marking thread as monitored.

vikram_runtime: leaving notes in the pool config and adding link to this thread in the change log.

marta_support: thanks all :heart:
